title: Reverse the Words
oneLiner: Split a sentence into words, reverse their order, and join them back with single spaces.
keyTakeaway: Split, transform, join is the everyday shape of text processing. Splitting on runs of spaces (Split with RemoveEmptyEntries in C#, split() with no argument in Python) takes care of extra spaces for you.
explanation:
Given a sentence, return the same words in reverse order, separated by single spaces. Extra spaces at the start, the end, or between words should disappear: "  hello   world " becomes "world hello". A sentence with no words gives an empty string. Words only contain letters; you're reversing the order of words, not the letters inside them.

Three steps. Split the sentence into a list of words: in C# text.Split(' ', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries) (without the option, double spaces produce empty strings), in Python text.split() with no argument, which splits on any run of whitespace. Reverse the list: Array.Reverse(words) or a loop from the end in C#, words[::-1] or reversed(words) in Python. Join with one space: string.Join(" ", words) or " ".join(words).

visualizationSteps.message: Input " start  the pump" has a leading space and a double space. A plain Split(' ') or split(" ") gives these five pieces, two of them empty.
Split with RemoveEmptyEntries (C#) or split() with no argument (Python) instead: the empty pieces are dropped, leaving three words.
Reverse the list of words. The letters inside each word stay as they are.
Join with single spaces: "pump the start".

complexity.note: Splitting, reversing and joining each touch every character a constant number of times; the list of words and the result hold O(n) characters.
